statements.impact_statement: CVE-2025-66413 is a Git for Windows advisory (GHSA-hv9c-4jm9-jh3x, https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/security/advisories/GHSA-hv9c-4jm9-jh3x). If a Windows user clones from a malicious server, Git may answer an NTLM challenge with the logged-on user's NTLMv2 hash, which can then be brute-forced. Git for Windows 2.53.0(2) fixed it by disallowing NTLM authentication by default (merge commit https://github.com/git-for-windows/git/commit/e9edee0b34751bf4d7d1feda0e2535bff64d4e77). Debian classes the CVE as NOT-FOR-US: Git for Windows (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-66413). The leak depends on Windows integrated authentication, which supplies the signed-in user's credentials without the user entering any. This owner is upstream Git for Linux (Alpine 3.23). Its published builds, 2.52.0-r0 and 2.52.1-r0 on x86_64 and aarch64, do HTTP authentication through libcurl. On Linux, libcurl's NTLM support uses only a user name and password that Git was given for that server, and the libcurl builds in the same repository (8.17.0 and later) no longer include the winbind single-sign-on helper, which curl removed in 8.8.0. A server can only obtain credentials the user has already supplied for it, and it could request those with Basic authentication anyway. Upstream Git has not adopted the Git for Windows default change; this decision rests on the platform, not on a code change.
